compatibility_decisions.reason: The 1.0 core capabilities add typed, fallible APIs without removing an already supported wire or persisted contract.
Runtime construction is fallible and must not hide initialization failure behind a panic-compatible constructor.
The old name claimed zero-copy behavior that the implementation never provided; the replacement states the ownership cost accurately.
The exported placeholder and production probe facades were replaced by narrow capabilities; test-only probes moved behind the explicit test-support feature.

The unreleased response aggregate is a validated remoting response, not an execution plan; the replacement aligns it with RemotingRequest and distinguishes construction failures from delivery failures without changing wire behavior.
The metadata accessor reports the response body representation, not a response execution plan; the unreleased name is corrected before the first production release.
The error class describes failure to construct a response, not a response value; the variant and low-cardinality label now identify that stage explicitly.
The observation records ResponseBodyKind rather than a plan category; the unreleased telemetry field is renamed with the corresponding accessor.

compatibility_decisions.old_item_path: rocketmq_store_rocksdb and rocketmq_tieredstore public RocketMQError/backend-error returns and raw constructors
compatibility_decisions.replacement: StoreError plus RocksDbOpenPlan/TieredStoreOpenPlan capability constructors returning Result<Option<_>, StoreError>
compatibility_decisions.reason: Unreleased backend APIs must preserve typed storage causes and represent pre-I/O capability validation without backend-specific public errors, panic, or default normalization.

frozen_contracts.behavior: MappedFileBuilder creates a usable mapped file for supported defaults and returns a typed configuration or I/O error for unsupported or invalid inputs.
One immutable server policy generation overrides server-owned gRPC settings while preserving client identity and subscription expressions.

The deprecated Classic Pull facade remains functional on the shared runtime, supports synchronous and asynchronous pull, queue discovery, offset persistence, listeners, and scheduled callbacks without advertising LitePull stream semantics.
